title: Kezem, Lábam, Fejem – Possessed Body Parts

sections.title: The same possessive suffixes, on a new set of nouns
sections.content: Body parts take the same possessive suffixes you already use for family and belongings — just applied to fej, kéz, láb, szem, fül and száj. Watch for one small twist: kéz ("hand") shortens its vowel before a suffix, so "my hand" is kezem, not kézem — the same kind of shortening you'll also hear in víz → vizet.

sections.title: "My" and "your" with fej, kéz and láb

items.spanish: Ez a kezem, az a lábam.
items.english: This is my hand, that is my leg.

items.spanish: A szeme kék, a füle kicsi.
items.english: His/her eye is blue, his/her ear is small.

sections.content: Hungarian doesn't usually bother saying "foot" and "leg" as two different words in everyday speech — láb covers both, and context (or fejtől lábig, "from head to toe") makes clear which part is meant.
